key_insight: A measurement-validated CFD workflow shows that dense urban building forms can significantly amplify rooftop wind for micro-turbines, especially when an architecturally integrated aerofoil is added at the envelope edge.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design-stage framework for placing building-integrated wind turbines on dense urban blocks, linking wind-rose conditions, building geometry, and turbine choice to expected energy yield.
method: Multi-month on-site anemometry on two Parisian case-study buildings
Calibrated steady-RANS CFD digital twin using the realizable k-epsilon turbulence model
Added an envelope-edge aerofoil to locally accelerate and stabilise flow
evidence_signal: Model validation against year-long anemometer records achieved about 18% MAPE and FAC2 above 0.85; the ENSAPVS case showed a 3.4x wind speed-up and an estimated 69 MWh/year yield.
watch_item: Results are based on steady-RANS and case-study-specific urban geometry, so transferability and year-to-year performance should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Assessment of wind energy potential of buildings by CFD simulation in dense urban environments - From Case Studies to a Dendrogram-Based Design Framework
